turns.answer:
I tried to summon the Concierge first, but a hook in this session blocks spawning agents ("Not available in this session"). So I read the pages myself and wrote nothing to the house.

**One tension, said once.** The palace argues against this exact move. The Quality Manifesto lists "optimized thumbnail/title (clickbait that works)" and "hooks in first 3 seconds" as *their* way of doing things (`Quality Manifesto.md:137`, `:141`). The channel's design rules say no hype and no "subscribe and hit the bell" (`_ops/loudon-live/design-system/README.md:61`). It's your channel, so I've followed you. The line I held is honesty: every hook below is true, and no title promises something the video doesn't deliver. If you want a bridge between the two, the manifesto's own Paradox section is one: reach that brings in the right people, who then become coaching clients.

**Where views actually come from.** The About page mostly gets read by people who have already clicked. The title and thumbnail decide whether someone clicks at all. The first 30 seconds decide whether YouTube keeps showing the video to others. That's general platform knowledge — I didn't check it today. So most of the effort below goes into the trailer and the titles.

---

## Tagline (banner)

> **Stop guessing at your sound.**
> Sound design, synthesis and music technique for electronic musicians.

## About

> Sound design, synthesis and music technique for electronic musicians — learned by building real instruments and effects, on video and live.
>
> I'm Loudon. I've taught music for twenty years. Here I take one project at a time and push it forward on camera, so you see all of it: the idea, the build, the part where it breaks, and the fix.
>
> What you'll find here:
> · Why a sound feels warm, wide or punchy — and how to get it there on purpose
> · Synths and effects built from first principles, in whatever tool fits: Max, RNBO, Ableton Live, code
> · Read The Manual: working through the entire Ableton Live 12 manual, section by section, testing every claim
> · Real music technique, not just producer tricks
>
> New videos every [DAY]. Live builds [DAY · TIME]. Subscribe and you'll catch the next one.
>
> One-on-one coaching: [link]

The first line is under 150 characters on purpose, because that's what shows in search results and the channel preview.

## Short bio

> Sound design and synthesis for electronic musicians, learned by building. New videos every [DAY].

## Trailer (~45 sec)

> *[Cold open — no logo, no hello. A thin, plain synth tone. One control moves, and it opens into something warm and wide. A beat of silence.]*
>
> That was one control. Most of us move it by feel. On this channel we find out what it's actually doing — and then we build our own.
>
> I'm Loudon, and this is Loud'n Live. I've taught music for twenty years. Here it's sound design, synthesis and music technique, for people who make electronic music.
>
> Every video pushes one real project forward. A synth from scratch. An effect worth putting on your next track. The whole Ableton Live 12 manual, every section tested, so you know what's really in there.
>
> Some of it's live, and some of it breaks on camera. That's usually where the good part is.
>
> New videos every [DAY]. Subscribe — and go make something.

## Titles and thumbnails (the biggest lever)

**Retitle after the stream.** Keep a live stream's title loose, because you don't know yet how it ends. Once it's a recording, rename it after what actually happened. A specific, true result with a question left open is honest, and it's what gets clicks.

- `I built a [thing] from scratch in [tool]`
- `Why [sound] feels [quality] — and the one control behind it` (only when it really is one control)
- `A sound that rises forever and never gets higher · building a Shepard tone synth`
- `A wavetable synth shaped like a donut` (the 2D Torus)
- Read The Manual: `Ableton Live 12 Compressor — every setting tested (RTM 28.14)`. Putting the feature first is what people search for, but it costs the series its clean numbered sorting (`Projects/LDN RTM.md:60`). That trade is yours to make.

**Thumbnails:** one big image (the instrument, the waveform, or your face), three words at most, high contrast. Put the Lissajous mark in the same corner every time so people recognize the channel in their feed.

**The first 30 seconds of every video:** start on the sound and say hello after it. The kit's current opening ("Hey, welcome in…") is where viewers leave.

---

**Flags:**
- **This breaks the channel's design rules.** It uses "you" hooks, "Stop guessing," subscribe asks and tool names up front, all of which the rules forbid. It still has no emoji, no hashtags and no promises a video can't keep. If you want this version to stand, the rules in `_ops/loudon-live/design-system/README.md` and `SKILL.md` need to change too. Otherwise the next agent that makes a card will quietly undo it. Changing those rules is an elder's write and needs your yes.
- **"Twenty years"** comes from `Quality Manifesto.md:203`. Please confirm the number.
- **The current launch kit is out of date.** It describes a stream-only channel and spells the name "Loudon Live." The rewrite follows the current entry instead: videos and streams, Read The Manual, and coaching (`Projects/Loudon Live.md:61-66`).

**Where it would go:** it would replace sections 1–3 of `Projects/Loudon Live/Loudon Live — launch kit.md`, and add the retitling rule to section 4. That file has frontmatter and links, so by the house rules the write goes through the Concierge, which isn't available in this session. Say **"grow up"** and I'll write it in, or keep it here and paste what you like.
